The token's metadata links a rewritten post by the same account, 69 seconds before creation.

Creation in one transaction, signed by the deployer and the mint key, slot 426930467: pays 84.740740739 SOL into the curve for 792,454,486.758954 tokens, total out 86.06810776 SOL. No Jito tip in the transaction.
The launch tool's fee account receives exactly 0.3 % of an 85.8 SOL input, 0.2574 SOL. The metadata is hosted by the same tool, uxento.io.
One second after creation the deployer already tries to give 100 % of creator fees to GV6UUmNx. That transaction fails.
650,000,000 tokens from the deployer to GV6UUmNx, 37 seconds after creation. GV6UUmNx does not sign.
The deployer sells its remaining 142,454,486.76 tokens in seven transactions over 9 seconds for 159.405670644 SOL. Net on trading: +73.34 SOL.
The fee setting succeeds at 21:07:55, with GV6UUmNx at 10,000 basis points. In the same transaction the deployer collects 0.4857 SOL of accrued fees for itself.
The deployer itself signs and pays the transactions that push ANSEM's creator fees to GV6UUmNx: 15.31 SOL at 21:11:00, 165.44 SOL on 22 June, without any signature from GV6UUmNx.

9ryBR3Sn is a bot that reacts in the same slot, 1,104 positions later: it buys the last 645,513 tokens, then triggers the migration and buys 30,077,097 tokens on the new pool. Cost 16.09 SOL, including 1.18 SOL of priority fees.
The first transaction GV6UUmNx ever signs is on 23 June, a purchase of another token. It first moves ANSEM on 28 June.
His post on airdropping the fees directed to his profile, 14:03:08 UTC on 27 June, reposted at 14:06:38. It quotes a suggestion from another account and names no token.
The first buy of 5 SOL or more after that post comes 23 seconds later: 11.0 SOL at 14:03:31.
He describes it as a community takeover, says not to send coins to his wallet, and reports about $7M airdropped.

The deployer had launched a first token named The Black Bull, symbol ANSEM, the same day at 15:45:50, 5 h 20 min before. All of it, 400 M tokens, and 100 % of its fees went to a different wallet, Dt4gYgAU.
Three examples of later launches: about 86 SOL bought and 650 M or more tokens to GV6UUmNx. Counts in evidence/followups.json.
A token transfer out of GV6UUmNx is not proof that he sent it. This one, to the deployer, is signed by a third wallet that holds a permanent delegate on the mint.
The deployer and FkCcgvCo exchange SOL in both directions from the deployer's first hours.
6,532.87 of the 21,022.09 SOL sent by GV6UUmNx goes through three short-lived wallets into high-volume wallets. None of the three receives from the deployer's side.
490 M ANSEM move from GV6UUmNx to a new wallet on 1 August, which a high-volume wallet funded about an hour earlier. Signed by GV6UUmNx.
Third parties name the deployer: Lookonchain on the 650 M transfer; others call yHCxHBEa the dev wallet of @Supermanonchain's token. These are claims, not proof.
An X search for his replies naming the five most cited accounts returns one post, to @Supermanonchain: when you stop vamping good projects. The post it answers cannot be read.
Before this launch, another account publicly proposed coining him and sending supply and fees to AVAZvHLR. The idea is public and older than GV6UUmNx.
Bubblemaps' public count of the airdrop.
In the posts saved here, he first names $ANSEM on 28 June at 12:01:43.
